note: Allow lists: only what is written here may be used. Every entry needs approved_by and approved_on from a dietitian before production (the readiness report counts the ones that are empty). allowed_in says where an entry may be used. Anything not listed is refused or sent to the review queue, never guessed.

recipe_sources.rule: A recipe with a 'source' must name one of these, and the source must be allowed in the running environment. In production every recipe needs a source.

entries.note: INDB is derived from ICMR-NIN data; development only until a licence or ownership is confirmed.

entries.note: Unverified transcription of a book for private circulation; development only until the dietitian has checked the import (book_ingredient_map.json).

cooking_methods.rule: A recipe or AI draft that names a 'method' must use one of these. A method not listed gets no calculation. Deep frying is left out on purpose: it needs a measured oil uptake from a reviewer first.

entries.calculation: weights as given, no cooking factor
sum of raw weights; energy and macros factor 1.0; vitamin and mineral retention from USDA (not used yet)

units.rule: Household units a recipe or food row may use. 'fixed_ml' is a real measure; other units need a food-specific gram weight from the food master (USDA portion data). A unit not listed is flagged, never guessed. Units taken from NIN tables are development only until NIN permission is confirmed.

ingredient_aliases.rule: In production every name in the food master (its name and aliases, Hindi and regional too) must be approved here for that food. In development unapproved names still work, so reviewers can see them in use. A name that is a proxy match is listed in black_lists.json until a better record is found.
